description: The hand-verified expected outcome for oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/near-trivy-results-null.json -- a document written under a KNOWN artifact name, carrying the exact member that name's writer is required to carry, whose value is null rather than the JSON array the count unit Results[] is. It states a HALT, not rows, despite the .rows.json suffix this folder's naming convention requires: the suffix names the folder's contract (one expected file per fixture), not the shape of every outcome. Every value below was derived by reading the fixture and the authored tables in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py, and each is asserted programmatically by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/test_shape_routing_negative.py rather than taken on trust. Where this file and shape.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.
tool_note: The tool IS resolved here, which is what distinguishes this fixture from expected/unknown-shape.rows.json: the name routing keys on is one of the nine, so the writer is known and only its document shape is wrong.
null_field_note: scanner_class and adapter are null rather than omitted, so a generic loader reads this file with the same keys as the positive expected files in this folder. They are null because the halt precedes adapter selection and row construction. trivy is additionally the one tool whose class is decided per record from the section array a record was read from, so no single class could stand here even if a row existed -- shape.py hands its adapter the PER_RECORD sentinel rather than a plausible default, and the sentinel refuses to be stringified.

fixture.authored_note: An authored document, not captured tool output. Its four envelope members are the ones a real Trivy 0.74.0 report carries around the finding sections -- SchemaVersion, ArtifactName, ArtifactType and Metadata -- with the values this run's invocation produces for a filesystem scan of the scan root (ArtifactName ".", ArtifactType "filesystem"). They are present so the refusal rests on Results alone: a thinner document would also be refused, and then the fixture would not establish which member decided it. Nothing in it is a finding, a secret, a credential or a token, it names no path at all, and no value in it is a measurement of anything.
fixture.why_this_document: It is the one document over which the two authorities that describe this shape could disagree. Trivy is written in Go, and Go marshals an unset slice as null rather than as [], so "Results": null is a shape a real writer can emit -- which is exactly why the contract must answer it once, in one direction, rather than have the declared signature refuse it while the envelope predicate admits it. It is also the sibling of malformed-trivy.json, whose Results is an object: the two together cover the wrong-container and the no-container-at-all forms of one present member.
fixture.why_it_is_not_named_trivy_json: This folder already holds fixtures/trivy.json, the captured positive fixture, so a second file cannot take that name. The negative test therefore routes this document under the artifact filename its writer uses (see routed_as below) rather than under the fixture's own filename, which resolves to no tool at all.

routed_as.subject: trivy.json
routed_as.second_subject_note: Both forms are asserted, because a run resolves the path form (shape.route_artifact over an entry in harness/artifacts/raw/) while a bare filename is what the authored tables hold. Only the filename component is read; neither path is opened, and no absolute path appears in this file or in the test.
routed_as.fixture_name_resolution_note: shape.resolve_tool("near-trivy-results-null.json") is None. Asserted by the test so the halt below cannot be passing for the wrong reason: routed under its own name this document would halt with shape.REASON_UNRECOGNIZED_ARTIFACT_NAME, a different condition owned by expected/unknown-shape.rows.json.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Recorded for parity with the positive expected files in this folder; no row below carries it, because rows is empty by expectation.

shape_detection.conjunction: isinstance(doc, Mapping) and doc.get("version") == "2.1.0" and isinstance(doc.get("runs"), list)
shape_detection.is_sarif_derivation: A mapping with no version key and no runs key: None == "2.1.0" is False and isinstance(None, list) is False, so both halves fail and the native shape test below is what decides this document's fate.

one_fail_closed_contract.statement: Results must be present AND be a JSON array. One contract, enforced identically by both authorities that describe this shape, so this document has one authoritative answer rather than two.
one_fail_closed_contract.envelope_predicate: shape._matches_trivy_envelope, reached through shape.matches_native_shape("trivy", doc) and through shape.route
one_fail_closed_contract.declared_signature: shape.NATIVE_SIGNATURES["trivy"], whose required_key is "Results" and whose required_key_type is shape.JSON_TYPE_ARRAY, reached through shape.matches_native_signature("trivy", doc)
one_fail_closed_contract.authority_note: AAP 0.5.4 names this shape's count unit Results[], requires an artifact matching neither the SARIF shape nor a known native shape to halt rather than be best-effort parsed, and states the reject-rather-than-infer principle. Refusal is therefore the direction the contract takes, and it is taken at the envelope: an adapter handed a document with none of the containers it walks reports zero rows, and an empty result set is indistinguishable from a clean scan.
one_fail_closed_contract.observed_type_matrix_note: Eight states of one member, with both authorities' verdicts recorded side by side. The two array rows are the control: a contract strict enough to refuse an empty array would halt every clean Trivy scan, which is the same class of wrong answer in the opposite direction. The other six agree on refusal, and the two verdicts agreeing in every row is what the drift assertion in the negative test checks -- a relaxation of either authority alone fails it by name.

native_signature.authority: normalize.shape.NATIVE_SIGNATURES["trivy"], derived from AAP 0.5.4's per-shape record-location table
native_signature.expected: a JSON object carrying "Results" whose value is a JSON array, each element one scanned target holding the finding sections. An empty array is legitimate
native_signature.expected_note: Recorded verbatim and asserted equal to the signature's own statement string, so this file cannot describe a requirement the implementation does not make.
native_signature.why_it_fails: The key is present, so a presence-only test passes this document, and its value is a legal JSON value, so nothing about it is broken at the parser level. It is not the required container: null where a JSON array is required, so the per-target elements the adapter walks and reconcile._count_trivy counts do not exist to be enumerated.
native_signature.what_is_deliberately_not_required: The signature reads nothing inside Results. An empty Results array is legitimate, a target carrying none of the three supported finding sections is legitimate, and the halt on a non-empty UNSUPPORTED section (Licenses, ExperimentalModifiedFindings) remains the trivy adapter's own -- this layer establishes only that the document is a Trivy report at all.

counting_traversal.note: This is the measured reason the halt has to exist. The independent traversal walks Results through its own sequence coercion, which yields nothing for a null member, so it returns zero -- and an adapter reading the same document would emit zero rows and zero rejections. Admitted, the identity would balance at 0 = 0 + 0 over a document that states no count unit, and parse status would read clean. AAP 0.5.4 requires a halt rather than a best-effort parse, and AAP 0.9.2 lists the condition among those that stop the run.
counting_traversal.traversal_unchanged: reconcile.py's traversal is deliberately not hardened into a second shape test: its value is that it shares no code and no judgement with the row builder. The refusal belongs one layer up, in shape.py, and belongs to both of that layer's authorities equally.

named_halt_requirement.statement: A KeyError, TypeError or AttributeError escaping a half-attempted parse is a FAILURE, not a pass: it carries no reason, names no artifact, quotes no expected signature and cannot be told apart from a defect in the normalizer itself. A null member is the value most likely to produce one of those instead of a decision, which is why the exact type is asserted with assertIs(type(error), shape.UnknownArtifactShape) and never with Exception.
named_halt_requirement.raised_by_the_shape_layer: The exception must come from normalize.shape.route or normalize.shape.route_artifact -- the module that owns the decision -- rather than from an adapter reached with a document whose shape was never established.

halt.reason_constant_alias: shape.REASON_NATIVE_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH is the same literal under the name the signature layer uses: one condition, two names, so a record quoting either reports one defect rather than two.
halt.reason_inventory: shape.HALT_REASONS, the closed set of four: unrecognized-artifact-name, unsupported-document-type, sarif-producer-artifact-not-sarif, native-shape-unrecognized.
halt.reason_note: Not the name reason: the name trivy.json resolves to trivy. Not the container reason: an object top level is a supported container. Not the producer reason: trivy is not one of the three SARIF producers. The halt is attributable to the document not being this writer's native shape.
halt.raised_before: any adapter module is named, imported or called, and before any record traversal of any kind

observed_attributes.stem_note: For this reason the stem carries the canonical tool identifier rather than a filename: the writer is known by the time the shape is tested.
observed_attributes.expectation_authority: shape.native_shape_requirement("trivy"), quoted verbatim into the halt. Recorded here as its authority rather than copied, for the same reason the nine canonical identifiers are not copied into this folder: shape.py owns the one wording, and a second copy is a copy that drifts. The negative test asserts the halt's expectation is identical to that function's return value.

message_must_carry: the observed structure where that signature required a container
halt.details_method: shape.UnknownArtifactShape.details() returns the same facts as a flat JSON-serialisable mapping, adding expected_artifacts, signature_tool, expected_signature and signature_observation. The test asserts json.dumps over it succeeds, because harness/artifacts/logs/normalize-run.json has to carry the halt record.

not_a_rejection.reject_classes_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_CLASSES tuple -- a closed set of ten class names, not copied here so the one authority cannot drift into two. paths.is_reject_class is the predicate the test calls.
not_a_rejection.statement: The stated outcome is a halt, not a counted rejection: a rejection is a per-record outcome inside an adapter that already owns its artifact, and this document never reaches an adapter. The test asserts the non-membership of the reason and the exception name over paths.REJECT_CLASSES programmatically.

parse.why_well_formedness_is_the_point: null is a legal JSON value, so nothing about this document is broken at the parser level and nothing in it looks wrong at a glance: the key is there, the envelope reads like Trivy's, and handing it on "in case the scan simply found nothing" feels harmless. It is precisely that document -- one that parses perfectly, carries a known artifact name and reads plausibly -- that tempts a best-effort parse. Malformed input is a different condition, owned by this folder's reject-*-malformed-record fixtures.

counts.raw_count_unit_note: Null rather than 0: a count unit is a property of a document of the right shape, and this document has none. What the traversal would return over it anyway is recorded above under counting_traversal.would_return, where it is evidence about the defect rather than a reconciliation figure.
counts.reconciliation_identity: not applicable -- the halt precedes any record traversal, so no count unit exists to reconcile against

rows_note: Explicitly empty, and empty for a different reason than a clean scan is empty: the pipeline stopped, it did not look and find nothing.
guarded_failure: Two authorities describing one shape can disagree, and the disagreement is invisible in the output. An envelope that admitted this document while the declared signature refused it would hand it to the trivy adapter, which enumerates nothing from a null member, emits zero rows and zero rejections and reports success; the independent counting traversal returns zero as well, so the identity balances at 0 = 0 + 0 and parse status reads clean -- while the signature layer's own recorded verdict in harness/artifacts/logs/normalize-run.json says the document was never that writer's shape. The required outcome is the named halt, from both authorities, over the one document that can tell them apart.

assertions: The fixture's sha256, byte size, top-level type, top-level keys and null Results value equal the values recorded here, so this file cannot drift from the document it describes.
json.load over the fixture succeeds: well-formedness is asserted, not assumed.
shape.is_sarif over the document is False.
shape.matches_native_shape("trivy", doc) is False -- the envelope refuses a present-but-null Results.
shape.matches_native_signature("trivy", doc) and shape.NATIVE_SIGNATURES["trivy"].matches(doc) are both False, so the envelope predicate and the declared signature agree: one document, one answer.
shape.NATIVE_SIGNATURES["trivy"].required_key is shape.TRIVY_RESULTS_KEY and its required_key_type is shape.JSON_TYPE_ARRAY, which is the contract both entry points enforce.
The two verdicts agree across all eight Results states in the observed type matrix, and the two array states route, so neither authority can be relaxed or over-tightened without a named failure.
shape.matches_native_shape is False for every one of the nine tools over this document, so no other writer's envelope claims it either.

shape.route over the document under the subject trivy.json raises shape.UnknownArtifactShape, and the raised type is exactly that class -- never a KeyError, TypeError or AttributeError from a half-attempted read of a null member.
shape.route_artifact over harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json and the same document raises the same reason, so both entry points halt.
error.reason equals shape.REASON_NATIVE_SHAPE_UNRECOGNIZED, is a member of shape.HALT_REASONS and is neither the name reason, the container reason nor the producer reason.
error.stem is trivy, error.sarif_detected is False, error.version is None, and error.top_level_keys and top_level_length are the ones recorded here.

error.expectation equals shape.native_shape_requirement("trivy"), error.expected_signature equals shape.NATIVE_SIGNATURES["trivy"].statement (recorded verbatim above), and error.signature_observation records required_key_type "array" beside observed_key_type "null".
json.dumps over error.details() succeeds, so the halt reaches harness/artifacts/logs/normalize-run.json without a re-render.
reconcile.count_records("trivy", doc) is 0 -- the false-clean this halt prevents, asserted rather than asserted about.
No adapter module is imported by the halting routing call.
The rows array is empty, the rejection total is 0, and neither the reason nor the exception name is a member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES.
shape.resolve_tool over the fixture's own filename is None, so the subject the test routes under is the artifact filename and not the fixture name.
negative_test_contract.mandated_direction_note: AAP 0.5.4 mandates a negative test asserting that a native artifact does not route to the SARIF adapter; that assertion is owned by the same test file over the captured native fixtures. This fixture covers the direction a single writer's own contract opens: the marker its per-shape table names is present, and the document is still not that writer's shape -- so the envelope predicate and the declared signature must refuse it together.

related_fixtures.the_captured_positive: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/trivy.json -- the report this document imitates, whose Results IS an array of three scanned targets and which routes normally. It satisfies the contract this document fails, which is what keeps the refusal from being a refusal of everything.
related_fixtures.the_wrong_container_sibling: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/malformed-trivy.json -- the same envelope with Results as an OBJECT keyed by target. Its member is a container of the wrong type; this one's member is no container at all. Neither substitutes for the other: a predicate testing truthiness admits the object and refuses the null, and a predicate testing presence admits both.
related_fixtures.the_legitimate_empty_report: A Trivy report carrying "Results": [] is the clean-scan control and routes normally. It is asserted inline in the negative test's minimal-envelope set and in the observed type matrix above rather than committed as a fixture, because it is one key wide.
related_fixtures.the_adapter_owned_halt: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/halt-trivy-section-not-an-array.json -- a document of the RIGHT shape whose finding section is not an array, which the trivy adapter halts on. The two halts are complementary and neither substitutes for the other: this layer establishes the shape, the adapter validates what is inside it.
related_fixtures.the_fall_through: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/unknown-shape.json -- a document under an UNRECOGNISED name, which halts for a different reason.
related_fixtures.note: Named so a reader can see which layer owns which failure. No fixture's outcome is inferred from another's, and each expected file states its own.

prohibitions_observed: No secret value, credential, token or redacted-secret placeholder appears in any field of this file or its fixture (this tree is committed to git). No finding is judged, nothing is deduplicated, and no tool's output is characterised against another's: this file describes one document's shape decision and the halt it must produce, and nothing else.
